sense: of the present or recent times

terms.comment: recentiōre memoriā, in more recent times.

terms.gloss: of this age, of our time
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.2: ā prīncipe hujus aetātis philosophōrum
Cic. Phil. 4.7: ex hodiernō ejus ēdictō (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. modern, contemporary, of this age, current
terms.comment: Of the present time in general only after Augustus (Lewis & Short); see current.
Late Latin, from modo, just now, as hodiernus from hodiē; classical writers say recēns or hujus aetātis.

phrases.latin: mihi quantō plūra recentium seu veterum revolvō, tantō magis lūdibria rērum mortālium cūnctīs in negōtiīs obversantur
phrases.english: the more I turn over the events of modern times and of old, the more the mockery of human affairs meets me in everything

phrases.latin: disces tū quidem ā prīncipe hujus aetātis philosophōrum
phrases.english: you will learn, of course, from the foremost philosopher of our time

sources: Lewis & Short: recens · Lewis & Short: aetas · Lewis & Short: hodiernus · Lewis & Short: modernus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. modern; modern, contemporary, of this age, current.
